hunks.baseline: “Come on, grow. Skeletons, skeletons…”
hunks.sol: > - Come on, grow. Skeletons, skeletons…

hunks.baseline: Every time I saw a Skeleton spring up like a bean sprout, happiness welled up in a corner of my heart.
hunks.sol: Every time I watched a Skeleton shoot up like a bean sprout, happiness welled up inside me.

hunks.baseline: *Is this what it feels like to be a farmer?*
hunks.sol: *Is this how farmers feel?*

hunks.baseline: What a bumper harvest. A truly magnificent harvest.
hunks.sol: What a bumper crop. What a harvest.

hunks.baseline: I smiled brightly and swung my sickle—no, my spear—to begin reaping.
hunks.sol: I beamed and swung my sickle—no, my spear—and began reaping.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton Warlord, forced to offer up his subordinates as EXP, muttered in a sorrowful voice.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton Warlord, now forced to offer up his subordinates as EXP, muttered sorrowfully.

hunks.baseline: > - Ah, my soldiers. Forgive your disloyal commander. To be caught in the schemes of a wicked human and erased without even getting to demonstrate your true strength…
hunks.sol: > - Ah, my soldiers. Forgive your disloyal commander. To fall prey to the schemes of a wicked human and be erased before you could demonstrate your true strength…

hunks.baseline: I was about to swing my spear at the next one when I suddenly stopped.
hunks.sol: I was about to swing my spear at the next one when I stopped.

hunks.baseline: He was supposed to be groveling, yet he glared at me and talked back. The anger of being demoted from commander of the great undead army to EXP factory manager seemed to have driven out his fear of destruction.
hunks.sol: He was supposed to be groveling, yet here he was glaring at me and talking back. Apparently, his fury at being demoted from commander of the great undead army to EXP factory manager had overcome his fear of Erasure.

hunks.baseline: > - I would rather be destroyed than offer my soldiers to you!
hunks.sol: > - I would rather be erased than offer my soldiers to you!

hunks.baseline: “Whether you get destroyed or not is for me to decide. More importantly, say what you said earlier again.”
hunks.sol: “Whether you get erased is for me to decide. More importantly, repeat what you said before that.”

hunks.baseline: “You said you hadn’t even shown your true strength, right?”
hunks.sol: “You said they didn’t get to show their true strength, right?”

hunks.baseline: “Come to think of it, you have one strange Skill. Something called Commander's Rally, or whatever.”
hunks.sol: “Come to think of it, you have some weird Skill. Commander’s Rally, or whatever it was.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, right. No wonder something felt off. I forgot about that.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, right. No wonder something felt off. I forgot all about it.”

hunks.baseline: I smiled brightly and patted the Warlord's skull.
hunks.sol: I beamed and stroked the Warlord’s skull.

hunks.baseline: The Warlord asked again, sounding genuinely baffled.
hunks.sol: The Warlord asked, sounding genuinely baffled.

hunks.baseline: > - Commander's Rally? Why?
hunks.sol: > - Commander’s Rally? Why?

hunks.baseline: “It raises their Levels when they get the buff. I need to squeeze out as much EXP as possible.”
hunks.sol: “The buff raises their Levels. I need to squeeze every last bit of EXP out of them.”

hunks.baseline: “So hurry up and use it. Depending on how you perform, I might even let you go.”
hunks.sol: “So hurry up and use it. If you do a good job, I might even let you go.”

hunks.baseline: “There’s a saying in the human world. A man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold. It means that a man always keeps his word.”
hunks.sol: “There’s a saying in the human world: a man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold. It means a man always keeps his word.”

hunks.baseline: > - A man who lost his mama? What a strange saying.
hunks.sol: > - A man who lost his mama is worth a thousand pieces of gold? What a strange saying.

hunks.baseline: “Why would he lose his mama? Making mom jokes now, you fucking bastard? Maybe I should just destroy you.”
hunks.sol: “Why would he lose his mama? Making mom jokes now, you fucking bastard? Maybe I should just erase you.”

hunks.baseline: > - Wait! There’s a crack in my bone! My bone!
hunks.sol: > - Wait! My bone—it’s cracking! My bone!

hunks.baseline: The Warlord’s green pupils shifted anxiously from side to side.
hunks.sol: The Warlord’s green pupils darted anxiously from side to side.

hunks.baseline: For a Skeleton, he displayed a surprisingly wide range of emotions. Before long, he finally managed to force out an answer.
hunks.sol: For a Skeleton, he displayed a surprisingly wide range of emotions. After a moment, he finally forced out an answer.

hunks.baseline: > - That’s right! Not obedience, but a contract mutually agreed upon by both parties!
hunks.sol: > - That is right! Not obedience, but a contract mutually agreed upon by both parties!

hunks.baseline: “…This bastard is more human than I am, despite being a Skeleton. So what are the terms of this contract?”
hunks.sol: “…This bastard is more human than I am, and he’s a Skeleton. So what are the terms?”

hunks.baseline: > - In exchange for cooperating with you, wicked human, guarantee the position I currently hold.
hunks.sol: > - In exchange for cooperating with you, wicked human, you will guarantee my current position.

hunks.baseline: “The master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army?”
hunks.sol: “As master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army?”

hunks.baseline: > - Correct! In addition, cease this indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter!
hunks.sol: > - Correct! In addition, you will cease this indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter!

hunks.baseline: To be told to stop indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter by a monster of all things left my head spinning for a moment.
hunks.sol: A monster, of all things, had just told me to stop my indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter. My head spun for a moment.

hunks.baseline: “Are you out of your mind? Is that something a monster is supposed to say?”
hunks.sol: “Are you out of your mind? Is that something a monster should be saying?”

hunks.baseline: > - How insulting. I am a Skeleton Warlord possessed of cool judgment and intelligence. Though I may have become a fallen undead, the spirit of chivalry is engraved deep within my soul.
hunks.sol: > - How insulting. I am a Skeleton Warlord possessed of cool judgment and intelligence. Though I may have become one of the fallen undead, the spirit of chivalry remains engraved deep within my soul.

hunks.baseline: “…If you had upheld chivalry, you wouldn’t have fallen like this in the first place.”
hunks.sol: “…If you’d upheld chivalry, you probably wouldn’t have fallen in the first place.”

hunks.baseline: > - …The truth is, my memories from when I was alive were erased when I became undead.
hunks.sol: > - …The truth is, my memories of life were erased when I became undead.

hunks.baseline: Still, perhaps because he was a Named Monster, he was definitely different from ordinary monsters that were consumed by instinct and did nothing but howl.
hunks.sol: Still, perhaps because he was a Named Monster, he was clearly different from ordinary monsters that were ruled by instinct and did nothing but howl.

hunks.baseline: I thought it over carefully before finally opening my mouth.
hunks.sol: I considered it carefully, then finally spoke.

hunks.baseline: As I watched the green light in his eyes shake in confusion, I continued.
hunks.sol: I continued as the green light in his eyes quivered with confusion.

hunks.baseline: “I’m okay with the first proposal. You can be the master of the Black Forest and the commander of the army, or whatever. But…”
hunks.sol: “The first demand is fine. You can be the master of the Black Forest, commander of the army, whatever you want. But…”

hunks.baseline: “From now on, you’re the Peace Guild’s EXP factory manager. In exchange for guaranteeing your position, supply me with as many Skeletons as I want.”
hunks.sol: “From now on, you’re the Peace Guild’s EXP factory manager. In exchange for guaranteeing your position, you’ll supply me with as many Skeletons as I want.”

hunks.baseline: > - That’s absurd!
hunks.sol: > - That is absurd!

hunks.baseline: > - I would rather be destroyed than become a human puppet!
hunks.sol: > - I would rather be erased than become a human puppet!

hunks.baseline: “Your wish has been received, valued customer.”
hunks.sol: “Your request has been received, valued customer.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton Warlord, a crack running across the crown of his skull, answered in a solemn voice.
hunks.sol: A crack spread across the crown of the Skeleton Warlord’s skull. He answered in a solemn voice.

hunks.baseline: > - A commander cannot abandon his soldiers. Human, as the master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army, I accept your proposal.
hunks.sol: > - A commander cannot abandon his soldiers. Human, as master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army, I accept your proposal.

hunks.baseline: “You said you’d rather be destroyed than become a human puppet.”
hunks.sol: “You just said you’d rather be erased than become a human puppet.”

hunks.baseline: > - When a commander disappears, the army falls apart. Do not misunderstand. I am merely enduring this momentary humiliation for the sake of the soldiers waiting for me.
hunks.sol: > - An army falls apart without its commander. Do not misunderstand. I am merely enduring a moment of humiliation for the sake of the soldiers waiting for me.

hunks.baseline: “But you have to offer up those very soldiers.”
hunks.sol: “But those are the very soldiers you have to offer up.”

hunks.baseline: > - I will remember their noble sacrifice until the day I am destroyed. So, how many troops is this month’s tribute—no, how many tribute troops do you require?
hunks.sol: > - I will remember their noble sacrifice until the day I am erased. So, how much is this month’s tribute? No—how many troops must I offer?

hunks.baseline: Look at him, giving them away without holding back since he wasn’t the one being destroyed.
hunks.sol: Look at him handing them over without a second thought now that he wasn’t the one being erased.

hunks.baseline: When I stared at him with an utterly dumbfounded expression, the world’s first pro-human Named Monster, the Skeleton Warlord, hurriedly began chanting.
hunks.sol: When I stared at him in utter disbelief, the world’s first pro-human Named Monster hurriedly began chanting.

hunks.baseline: The harvest was easy.
hunks.sol: The harvesting was easy.

hunks.baseline: The first time was difficult, but after doing it two or three times, I got the hang of it.
hunks.sol: The first time was the hard part. After two or three repetitions, I got the hang of it.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton Warlord made full use of his abilities as a commander to fill his tribute ranks as quickly as possible.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton Warlord made full use of his abilities as a commander to gather the tribute troops as quickly as possible.

hunks.baseline: > - Army! Rally together!
hunks.sol: > - Legion! Assemble!

hunks.baseline: Around a hundred newly grown Skeletons gathered in one place. All I had to do was scatter Spear Energy at the monsters that had gathered at his command, and EXP came pouring down.
hunks.sol: Around a hundred freshly sprouted Skeletons gathered in one place. All I had to do was unleash Spear Energy at the monsters assembled under his command, and EXP came raining down.

hunks.baseline: The sound of EXP being deposited made the corners of my mouth rise. Watching the scene, the Warlord muttered in a satisfied voice.
hunks.sol: The sound of EXP rolling in brought a smile to my face. As he watched, the Warlord muttered in satisfaction.

hunks.baseline: > - Human. Did you see my command ability? This is the dignity of a commander.
hunks.sol: > - Human. Have you witnessed my command ability? This is the majesty of a commander.

hunks.baseline: Watching him take pride in discovering an efficient way to offer up his soldiers, I felt like I finally understood why his soul had become corrupted.
hunks.sol: Watching him take pride in devising a more efficient way to offer up his soldiers, I felt like I finally understood why his soul had become corrupted.

hunks.baseline: If the winds of liberation ever swept through the Black Forest, the Skeleton independence fighters would put him at the top of their purge list.
hunks.sol: If the winds of liberation ever swept through the Black Forest, the Skeleton independence fighters would put him at the very top of their purge list.

hunks.baseline: *This is giving me the strange feeling that I’m the invader.*
hunks.sol: *Why do I feel like I’m the invader here?*

hunks.baseline: Feeling oddly unsettled, I began collecting the loot.
hunks.sol: Feeling strangely conflicted, I began collecting the loot.

hunks.baseline: Skeletons were one of the most dirt-poor monster species around. Their so-called by-products were either rusty weapons that could cause tetanus or half-rotted bones.
hunks.sol: Skeletons were among the most penniless monsters around. Their so-called by-products consisted of rusty weapons that could give you tetanus and half-rotted bones.

hunks.baseline: You could at least get beef and bone broth from a Minotaur corpse. Apparently, no matter how long you simmered these, all you got was the taste of a grave.
hunks.sol: You could at least get beef and bone broth from a Minotaur carcass. Apparently, no matter how long you simmered Skeleton bones, all you got was the taste of a grave.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, a Magic Gem and some Equipment.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, a Magic Gem and some armor.”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: At least Skeleton Knights, which appeared about as often as beans in a drought, sometimes left behind one or two Magic Gems and decent pieces of Equipment, like this.
hunks.sol: At least Skeleton Knights, which appeared about as often as beans in a drought, sometimes left behind one or two Magic Gems and decent pieces of Equipment like these.

hunks.baseline: Of course, even that only happened once in a while.
hunks.sol: Of course, even that only happened once in a blue moon.

hunks.baseline: “With a Magic Gem this size, it should easily fetch tens of millions of won.”
hunks.sol: “A Magic Gem this size should easily fetch tens of millions of won.”

hunks.baseline: It had been a good decision to send the Guild members away. I got to monopolize the EXP and the Magic Gems too—the best of both worlds.
hunks.sol: Sending the Guild members away had been the right call. I got to monopolize both the EXP and the Magic Gems—the best of both worlds.

hunks.baseline: As I happily pocketed a Magic Gem the size of an adult’s fist, the Warlord asked me a question.
hunks.sol: As I happily pocketed a Magic Gem the size of a grown man’s fist, the Warlord asked,

hunks.baseline: “You can see what I’m doing. I’m collecting the rewards for my labor.”
hunks.sol: “Can’t you tell? Collecting the fruits of my labor.”

hunks.baseline: “Absorb it? Don’t be ridiculous. Of course I’m selling it.”
hunks.sol: “Absorb it? Don’t be ridiculous. Of course I’m going to sell it.”

hunks.baseline: > - Foolish. Magic Gems are the source of power. Is it not only natural to eat them and grow stronger?
hunks.sol: > - Foolish. Magic Gems are the source of power. Is it not only natural to consume them and grow stronger?

hunks.baseline: It was already well known, but humans were not monsters’ only enemies.
hunks.sol: It was common knowledge that humans weren’t monsters’ only enemies.

hunks.baseline: It was perfectly normal for monsters to fight among themselves, and some even ate enemy monsters to grow stronger in the process.
hunks.sol: Monsters often fought among themselves, and some grew stronger by devouring the monsters they defeated.

hunks.baseline: > - Is that so? Humans are truly an incomprehensible lot. You could become stronger by absorbing Magic Gems… Is money really so wonderful?
hunks.sol: > - Is that so? Humans are truly an incomprehensible race. You could grow stronger by absorbing Magic Gems… Is this thing called money really so wonderful?

hunks.baseline: “Money is something we need whether we like it or not, to get by. Besides, humans can’t absorb Magic Gems.”
hunks.sol: “We need money to live whether we like it or not. Besides, humans can’t absorb Magic Gems.”

hunks.baseline: The energy contained in Magic Gems was commonly called demonic qi. It was the foundation of a monster’s strength, but to humans, it was no different from poison.
hunks.sol: The energy contained within Magic Gems was commonly known as demonic qi. It was the foundation of a monster’s strength, but to humans, it was no different from poison.

hunks.baseline: It was a type of qi, but it was easier to understand if you thought of it as a contaminant.
hunks.sol: It was a type of qi, but the easiest way to understand it was to think of it as a contaminant.

hunks.baseline: > - You cannot absorb it? That is strange. The human group I encountered long ago used Troll blood to heal their bodies.
hunks.sol: > - You cannot absorb it? How strange. A group of humans I encountered long ago used Troll blood to heal their bodies.

hunks.baseline: “Ah, potions? That undergoes a purification process…”
hunks.sol: “Ah, potions? That goes through a purification process…”

hunks.baseline: > - Then why not purify Magic Gems? Just as you do with the Troll blood you call potions.
hunks.sol: > - Then why not purify Magic Gems as well? Just as you do with the Troll blood you call potions.

hunks.baseline: “If it were that simple, we would have purified them long ago. You really are simple, just like a monster.”
hunks.sol: “If it were that simple, we’d have purified them long ago. You really are simpleminded, just like a monster.”

hunks.baseline: If Troll blood was a fruit-flavored drink with one percent fruit flavoring, then a Magic Gem was one hundred percent fresh fruit juice.
hunks.sol: If Troll blood was a fruit-flavored drink with one percent fruit flavoring, a Magic Gem was one hundred percent fresh fruit juice.

hunks.baseline: People couldn’t even remove all the poison from potions, yet this guy was suggesting that they absorb Magic Gems.
hunks.sol: People couldn’t even remove all the toxicity from potions, yet he was suggesting we absorb Magic Gems.

hunks.baseline: “Stop asking questions, you question-mark murderer. That’s the established academic consensus. I’ve never heard or seen anything like that.”
hunks.sol: “Stop asking questions, you question-mark murderer. That’s the accepted academic consensus. No one’s ever heard of anything like that.”

hunks.baseline: *Wait. That actually makes sense.*
hunks.sol: *Wait. He has a point.*

hunks.baseline: *There’s no need to be bound by common sense all the time.*
hunks.sol: *There’s no reason to be bound by common sense.*

hunks.baseline: Was I not an existence beyond common sense myself?
hunks.sol: Wasn’t I living proof that common sense didn’t apply to everything?

hunks.baseline: The phrase *established academic consensus* merely referred to a conclusion drawn from what was known.
hunks.sol: Even the so-called accepted academic consensus was only a conclusion based on what people currently knew.

hunks.baseline: *The Mana Cultivation Method was the same.*
hunks.sol: *The Mana Cultivation Method is the same.*

hunks.baseline: I had never thought about it before getting entangled with the Ares Guild.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t even considered that before getting tangled up with the Ares Guild.

hunks.baseline: Before monsters appeared and after they did, their private league had remained unchanged, and their secrets had continued to be shared within the boundaries they had established.
hunks.sol: Their private league had remained unchanged both before and after the appearance of monsters, and its secrets had always been shared only within the boundaries they had drawn.

hunks.baseline: *Should I try it once?*
hunks.sol: *Should I give it a try?*

hunks.baseline: Just as I was about to open my Inventory and take out another Magic Gem, the Warlord spoke.
hunks.sol: Just as I opened my Inventory to take the Magic Gem back out, the Warlord spoke.

hunks.baseline: > - Heh heh. You look like you just got punched. Wicked and foolish human.
hunks.sol: > - Heh heh. You look as though you have just been struck. Wicked and foolish human.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “Oh. Do you want me to give your skull an Annihilation Punch?”
hunks.sol: “Oh. Want me to hit your skull with an Erasure Punch?”

hunks.baseline: > - …A rash remark. I apologize.
hunks.sol: > - …That was a rash remark. I apologize.

hunks.baseline: “You apologized within three seconds, so I’ll let it slide.”
hunks.sol: “You apologized within three seconds, so I’ll allow it.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton Warlord, having avoided destruction by the universal rule, muttered.
hunks.sol: Having escaped Erasure by observing the universal three-second rule, the Skeleton Warlord muttered,

hunks.baseline: > - There is no greater humiliation. Consider yourself fortunate that I have not grown stronger, human.
hunks.sol: > - What humiliation. Count yourself fortunate that I did not grow any stronger, human.

hunks.baseline: “For a Skeleton Knight, becoming the master of the Black Forest through a coup was quite a career.”
hunks.sol: “You started as a Skeleton Knight and became master of the Black Forest through a coup. I’d say you’ve risen pretty far.”

hunks.baseline: > - I am a Warlord now! The master of the Black Forest and—
hunks.sol: > - I am a Warlord now! Master of the Black Forest and—

hunks.baseline: I only learned later that he had taken over the Black Forest.
hunks.sol: I had only learned later that he had taken over the Black Forest.

hunks.baseline: He had actually defeated the black wizard, who was practically the forest’s true master. He must have absorbed a truly incredible amount of Magic Gems.
hunks.sol: He had defeated the black wizard, who had practically been its true master. He must have absorbed an incredible number of Magic Gems.

hunks.baseline: “So this is a complete human—or rather, Skeleton—victory. Going from an ordinary Skeleton Knight to the master of the Black Forest, and even evolving into a Warlord… You must have absorbed an enormous number of Magic Gems from the black wizard, right?”
hunks.sol: “So this was a complete human—or rather, Skeleton—victory. You went from an ordinary Skeleton Knight to master of the Black Forest and even evolved into a Warlord. The Magic Gem you absorbed from the black wizard must have been incredible, right?”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: > - What are you talking about? He did not possess any Magic Gems.
hunks.sol: > - What are you talking about? He possessed no Magic Gem.

hunks.baseline: > - Besides, the black wizard was the one who summoned me directly. Until recently, his commands were absolute. A summoned creature cannot disobey its summoner.
hunks.sol: > - Besides, the black wizard was the one who summoned me directly. Until recently, his commands were absolute. A summoned creature cannot defy its summoner.

hunks.baseline: “Then how…”
hunks.sol: “Then how…?”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton Warlord’s green pupils narrowed.
hunks.sol: The green light in the Skeleton Warlord’s eyes narrowed.

hunks.baseline: > - I do not know the reason myself. Not long ago, I suddenly felt that I had escaped his control. Perhaps you could say that I climbed one step higher when my magical power surpassed that of my summoner.
hunks.sol: > - I do not know the reason myself. Not long ago, I suddenly realized that I had escaped his control. Perhaps one could say that my magical power had surpassed my summoner’s, allowing me to ascend to the next stage.

hunks.baseline: > - Yes. My magical power grew tremendously, all at once.
hunks.sol: > - Yes. My magical power increased tremendously, all at once.

hunks.baseline: What was he talking about?
hunks.sol: What the hell was he talking about?

hunks.baseline: Yet, just as the Warlord said, he could not properly explain what had happened to him either.
hunks.sol: But just as the Warlord said, even he couldn’t properly explain what had happened to him.

hunks.baseline: After thinking about it for a long while, the only thing he added was this:
hunks.sol: After thinking for a long time, he managed to add only one thing.

hunks.baseline: > - Borrowing a human expression, it felt as if I had been possessed by a ghost.
hunks.sol: > - To borrow a human expression, it felt as though I had been bewitched by a ghost.

hunks.baseline: “…Is that something a Skeleton can say?”
hunks.sol: “…Is that something a Skeleton should say?”

hunks.baseline: *Maybe that bastard isn’t a Skeleton after all.*
hunks.sol: *Maybe that bastard isn’t actually a Skeleton.*

hunks.baseline: It was at that moment, as I stared at the Warlord with an incredulous expression, that—
hunks.sol: Just as I stared at the Warlord in disbelief—

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The Warlord’s skull rolled around atop his neck before stopping in one direction.
hunks.sol: The Warlord’s skull rolled around atop his neck, then stopped facing one direction.

hunks.baseline: Looking south with his green pupils shining, he clicked his jawbones and spoke.
hunks.sol: The green light in his eyes shone as he gazed south and clacked his jaw.

hunks.baseline: > - An intruder.
hunks.sol: > - Intruders.

hunks.baseline: “An intruder?”
hunks.sol: “Intruders?”

hunks.baseline: > - I am the master of the Black Forest. I know everything that happens within the forest. More wicked humans have just set foot in my territory.
hunks.sol: > - I am master of the Black Forest. I know everything that happens within it. More wicked humans have just set foot in my territory.

hunks.baseline: After enthusiastically smacking him across the back of the head, I picked up the Warlord’s skull and started walking toward the Gate entrance.
hunks.sol: I gave the back of his head a hearty smack, picked up the Warlord’s skull, and headed toward the Gate entrance.
